biography.plain_text: Ira J. Kaufman was an American investment banker and Chicago business leader who chaired Rodman & Renshaw and Exchange Bancorp. He led a group of investors that acquired Exchange National Bank. During his chairmanship, Exchange agreed to merge with LaSalle, intending to expand the combined bank's commercial and international banking services.

long_biography.plain_text:
Chicago investment banker Ira Kaufman helped secure a future for the threatened Chicago Theatre. In 1985, he and fellow Rodman & Renshaw executive Bruce Young authorised their firm's participation in a rescue project. Its task was to raise private equity for a partnership involving the city administration.

The brokerage's sales team found the investors needed to supply $10 million in roughly a month. That financing enabled the acquisition of the theatre and adjoining Page Building, followed by restoration. The work took less than eleven months, and Frank Sinatra performed at the theatre's reopening in 1986.
